title: HDR interface: elements brighter than white
blurb: A panel drawn into a 16-bit float canvas. A badge, a focus ring and a progress bar take values above standard white from CSS colours, and the canvas multiplies a button and a dot after drawing them. Views show the extra range on a standard screen.
question: Do CSS colour values above 1.0 survive drawElementImage() into a float16 canvas, and which canvas operations and graphics routes keep them?
result: In a float16 Display P3 2D canvas, CSS colours above 1.0 read back unchanged, including box-shadow blur. multiply fills and fill shadows keep them; lighter, ctx.filter, CSS filter and drawImage() clamp to 1.0. WebGL and WebGPU element copies clamp to 1.0. On Chrome 159 on an Android phone the 2D canvas showed no extra brightness; a WebGPU rgba16float canvas with a shader that raises the uploaded element is the second route.
